sentences.text: GPS gives your position from satellite signals, typically accurate to within a few meters, and better with WAAS, a correction system available across North America.
A GPS receiver also gives speed over ground and course over ground, which come from changes in position, not from the compass.
Make sure the receiver’s datum matches your chart, normally WGS 84 matched to NAD 83.
GPS can fail, lose power or be jammed, so a good captain keeps dead reckoning skills, paper charts and a compass as backups.
The Loran system that once backed up GPS was shut down in 2010.
